ai.literal: Difficulty it possesses, saying, not losing heart is needed; greatness, effort will give.
ai.translation: One should not lose heart thinking a task is too difficult. Effort will grant the greatness needed to achieve it.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயல் செய்வதற்கு கடினமானது என்று எண்ணி மனம் தளராமல் இருக்க வேண்டும். அதைச் செய்து முடிக்கும் பெருமையை ஒருவரது முயற்சியே தந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises against giving up on a task just because it seems too difficult to accomplish. The word 'அசாவாமை' means not growing weary or losing heart when facing a challenge. Instead of feeling inadequate, one must realize that 'முயற்சி' (effort) itself will provide the 'பெருமை' (greatness or capability) required to succeed. The focus is on action and perseverance rather than the initial difficulty of the goal.

ai.literal: In action, effort failing guard against; unfinished action from those who abandoned, it has departed, the world.
ai.translation: Guard against your effort failing in the midst of a task. The world abandons those who abandon a task unfinished.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்யும்போது இடையில் முயற்சி குறைந்துவிடாமல் காக்க வேண்டும். செய்து முடிப்பதற்கு முன்பே செயலை விட்டு விலகியவர்களை விட்டு உலகமும் விலகிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against losing momentum or giving up while a task is underway. The phrase 'வினைக்கண் வினை கெடல் ஓம்பல்' urges one to guard against the failure of effort in the middle of an action. The word 'தீர்ந்தாரின்' means 'from those who have abandoned', referring to people who leave a task incomplete ('வினைக்குறை'). Just as they abandon their work, the world ('உலகு') will abandon them, denying them success and recognition.

ai.literal: Industriousness called excellence-in rests-indeed beneficence called greatness.
ai.translation: The noble pride of being a benefactor rests entirely on the excellent quality of industriousness.
ai.modern: பிறருக்கு உதவி செய்யும் வேளாண்மை என்னும் பெருமிதம், ஒருவருடைய விடாமுயற்சி என்னும் உயர்ந்த பண்பின் மேலேயே நிலைபெற்றுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: This couplet connects the capacity to help others with the habit of hard work. The word 'vēḷāṇmai' refers to beneficence or philanthropy, while 'tāḷāṇmai' means relentless effort or industriousness. The poet explains that the noble pride ('cerukku') of being a benefactor rests entirely on the excellent foundation of personal effort. Without working hard to gather resources, one cannot experience the greatness of giving to those in need. Here, 'cerukku', which often means arrogance, is used positively to denote the dignified joy of helping others.

ai.literal: effort he who lacks generosity coward hand sword-wielding like will fail
ai.translation: The generosity of a man who lacks industrious effort will fail, just like a sword wielded in the hand of a coward.
ai.modern: முயற்சி இல்லாதவன் பிறருக்கு உதவி செய்ய நினைப்பது, ஒரு பேடியின் கையில் உள்ள வாள் வீரம் பயன்படாமல் போவதைப் போல வீணாகிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares a lazy person's desire to be generous with a coward holding a sword. Just as a coward cannot actually fight despite holding a weapon, a person without industrious effort cannot sustain their generosity. The word தாளாண்மை means relentless effort, while வேளாண்மை here refers to the helpfulness or generosity that requires wealth generated by such effort. Without the former, the latter is merely an illusion and will ultimately fail.

ai.literal: Pleasure he-desires-not, work he-who-desires, his relatives' sorrow having-wiped-away supporting pillar.
ai.translation: He who desires not personal pleasure but desires to accomplish his work is a pillar that wipes away the sorrows of his kin and supports them.
ai.modern: தனக்குரிய இன்பத்தை விரும்பாமல், தான் செய்ய வேண்டிய செயலைச் செய்து முடிக்க விரும்புகின்றவன், தன் உறவினர்களின் துன்பத்தைப் போக்கி அவர்களைத் தாங்கும் தூண் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the character of a truly industrious person. It contrasts the rejection of personal pleasure with a deep dedication to one's work. Such a person becomes the foundational support for their family and community. The poet uses the metaphor of a pillar to show how this individual bears the weight of others' burdens, actively wiping away their sorrows. By prioritizing duty over comfort, the person provides strength and stability to their kindred.

ai.literal: Effort wealth will create; effort's lack poverty having thrust will leave.
ai.translation: Effort creates wealth. A lack of effort will thrust one into poverty.
ai.modern: முயற்சி ஒருவனுக்குச் செல்வத்தை உண்டாக்கும். முயற்சி இல்லாத நிலை அவனை வறுமையில் தள்ளிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the direct outcomes of diligence and laziness. The word 'முயற்சி' (effort) is paired with 'திரு' (wealth), showing that continuous action naturally generates prosperity. Conversely, a lack of effort brings about 'இன்மை' (poverty). The strong verb phrase 'புகுத்தி விடும்' (will thrust into) emphasizes the inevitable and forceful way that idleness plunges a person into destitution.

ai.literal: In laziness she dwells, the great goddess of misfortune, they say; laziness he who is without, in effort he who is, [his is] she of the lotus.
ai.translation: They say the great goddess of misfortune dwells in laziness. The goddess of the lotus belongs to the man who is free from laziness and steadfast in effort.
ai.modern: சோம்பலில் மூதேவி குடியிருப்பாள் என்று சான்றோர் கூறுவர். ஆனால், சோம்பல் இன்றி முயற்சியில் நிலைத்திருப்பவனிடம் தாமரையில் வீற்றிருக்கும் திருமகள் தங்கியிருப்பாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the outcomes of laziness and industriousness using personified imagery. The poet states that the goddess of misfortune ('முகடி') resides in laziness, bringing ruin to the idle. In contrast, the goddess of prosperity, who sits on a lotus ('தாமரையினாள்'), favors the one who is free from laziness and actively engaged in effort. The parallel structure emphasizes that wealth and success are naturally drawn to continuous hard work.

ai.literal: Fortune lack to anyone blame is not; knowledge having known effort lack blame.
ai.translation: Lacking good fortune is no disgrace to anyone. The true disgrace is lacking the effort to do what one knows must be done.
ai.modern: ஒருவருக்கு நல்லூழ் இல்லாதிருப்பது அவருக்குப் பழியாகாது; ஆனால் அறிய வேண்டியவற்றை அறிந்து அதற்கேற்ப முயற்சி செய்யாமல் இருப்பதே பழியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the lack of good fortune with the lack of effort. The word 'poṟi' can mean sense organs or destiny; here, contrasted with 'āḷviṉai' (effort), it means favorable fortune or destiny. The poet states that not being blessed with good fortune is not a fault or disgrace for anyone. However, failing to exert effort after understanding what needs to be done is a true disgrace. The emphasis is entirely on human agency and industry over innate luck.

ai.literal: By fate will not happen even if, effort one's own body to exert wages will give.
ai.translation: Even if fate prevents success, effort will still pay the wages for one's physical exertion.
ai.modern: விதியால் ஒரு செயல் நிறைவேறாது போனாலும், ஒருவருடைய முயற்சியானது அவரது உடல் உழைப்பிற்கு ஏற்ற பலனைத் தவறாமல் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute value of hard work, regardless of destiny or external forces. Even if fate dictates that a task cannot be accomplished, the effort itself is never wasted. The exertion of one's own body will always yield a proportional reward, ensuring that true industry is its own guarantee of return.

ai.literal: Even fate, the back they will see, weariness without, without slackening, those who strive.
ai.translation: Those who strive tirelessly and without slackening will see the back of even fate.
ai.modern: சோர்வில்லாமலும் தாமதிக்காமலும் தொடர்ந்து முயற்சி செய்பவர்கள், விதியையும் தோற்றுப் புறமுதுகு காட்டி ஓடச் செய்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme power of relentless human effort. The word 'உஞற்றுபவர்' refers to those who strive continuously, doing so 'உலைவு இன்றி' (without weariness) and 'தாழாது' (without slackening or delaying). The striking image here is 'உப்பக்கம் காண்பர்', which literally means seeing the back of an opponent in retreat. Thus, the text asserts that unwavering perseverance can make even 'ஊழ்' (fate or destiny) turn its back and flee.
